title: Glycan-specific whole cell affinity chromatography: A versatile microbial adhesion platform
author: Van Tassell, Price, et al.

steps.title: Dissolve glycan in buffer
steps.instruction: In a glass screw‑cap tube, dissolve 0.3 mmol of the desired glycan in 1 mL of sodium bicarbonate buffer.

steps.title: Add acetyl acetone
steps.instruction: Add 35 µL of acetyl acetone (≈1.1:1 molar ratio to glycan) and vortex to dissolve.

steps.title: Heat reaction mixture
steps.instruction: Seal the tube and incubate in a water bath or heating block at 80–90 °C for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Cool and vent tube
steps.instruction: Remove the tube, allow it to cool to ambient temperature, and vent slowly to release any CO₂ pressure before opening. A slight yellow‑brown discoloration may appear, especially with larger or more complex glycans.

steps.title: Extract with ethyl acetate
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL ethyl acetate, shake to mix, allow the phases to separate, and discard the upper ethyl acetate layer. If separation is slow, place the reaction in a freezer for 10–15 min to aid separation.

steps.title: Neutralize aqueous phase
steps.instruction: To the aqueous phase add acid ion‑exchange resin 10–20 mg at a time, shaking gently to release CO₂; continue adding resin until gas evolution stops.

steps.title: Collect C‑glycoside ketone solution
steps.instruction: Remove the aqueous phase from the resin and retain it (C‑glycoside ketone formation may be verified by mass spectrometry at this stage if desired).

steps.title: Prepare hydrazide resin
steps.instruction: In a glass vial, place 1 mL (bed volume) of hydrazide resin and wash with water to remove the storage buffer.

steps.title: Load ketone onto resin
steps.instruction: Remove excess water from the resin and add 200 µL of the C‑glycoside ketone solution.

steps.title: Evaporate excess liquid
steps.instruction: Under a gentle air stream, evaporate the majority of the aqueous phase from the resin, taking care not to displace the resin from the vial.

steps.title: Incubate resin in pyridine
steps.instruction: Dilute the resin in 2 mL pyridine, vortex to mix, and incubate at ambient temperature for at least 1 h.

steps.title: Remove pyridine and wash resin
steps.instruction: Carefully remove pyridine with a Pasteur pipette, then wash the resin 5–6 times with 3–4 resin volumes of water to eliminate all pyridine.

steps.title: Store or use functional resin
steps.instruction: Retain the resin for immediate use or suspend it in 0.02 % sodium azide and store at 4 °C; the resin remains functional for longer than two months.

steps.title: Hydrolyze resin with TFA
steps.instruction: Place 150 µL of resin in a glass vial, add 0.5 mL of 2 N TFA, and heat at 120 °C for 30 min on a heating block.

steps.title: Derivatize with hydroxylamine
steps.instruction: Evaporate the reaction to dryness on an airline, then add 0.5 mL saturated hydroxylamine HCl in pyridine and incubate for 20 min at 60 °C.

steps.title: Acetylate to aldononitrile acetate
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL acetic anhydride, react for 20 min at 60 °C, evaporate (in a fume hood), re‑dissolve in ethyl acetate, back‑extract with water, remove the upper ethyl acetate layer and analyze by GC/MS.

steps.title: Equilibrate lectin column
steps.instruction: Place 100 µL (bed volume) of mannose‑C‑glycoside resin in a stoppered 1 mL spin column and wash three times with 0.5 mL lectin buffer.

steps.title: Incubate resin with fluorescent lectin
steps.instruction: In the dark, incubate the column for 10 min at ambient temperature with 200 µL lectin buffer containing 10 µg fluorescein‑conjugated lectin.

steps.title: Wash unbound lectin
steps.instruction: Unstop the column and allow unbound lectin to flow out by gravity (≈2–5 min); collect this flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash and elute bound lectin
steps.instruction: Collect the flow‑through together with three 200 µL washes of lectin buffer, then perform three 200 µL elutions with lectin buffer containing 200 mM mannose.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence of fractions
steps.instruction: Measure fluorescence intensity of each collected sample using a FLx800 Fluorescence Microplate Reader; excess fluorescence in elution fractions relative to washes indicates lectin binding and release.

steps.title: Grow bacterial cultures to exponential phase
steps.instruction: Grow E. coli K12 aerobically in BHI at 37 °C, 200 rpm shaking to OD₆₀₀ = 0.8–1.0; grow C. jejuni 11168 as a lawn on Mueller‑Hinton blood agar (5 % bovine blood) under microaerophilic conditions at 37 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Prepare columns for bacterial assay
steps.instruction: Prepare columns as in the lectin affinity procedure, washing three times with 0.5 mL PBS to equilibrate before each test; optional pre‑blocking with BSA is unnecessary for these bacteria.

steps.title: Harvest and wash bacteria
steps.instruction: For K12, centrifuge culture at 3000 × g for 3 min, resuspend in PBS, repeat twice. For Cj11168, scrape colonies with a sterile loop, suspend in PBS, vortex briefly, centrifuge at 3000 × g for 5 min, resuspend in PBS, repeat twice.

steps.title: Standardize inoculum density
steps.instruction: Adjust both K12 and Cj11168 to OD₆₀₀ = 0.50 ± 0.01 (≈4 × 10⁸ CFU/mL), then dilute to obtain approximately 2 × 10⁵ CFU/mL.

steps.title: Combine inocula with test competitors
steps.instruction: For each 0.5 mL inoculum aliquot, add either 100 mM mannose, 100 mM galactose, 40 mg/mL yeast mannan, or PBS (control) for K12; or 10 mg/mL 2‑fucosyllactose (2FL), 10 mg/mL lactose, or PBS (control) for Cj11168.

steps.title: Apply bacterial inocula to columns
steps.instruction: Add the inoculum mixture to the column and incubate until the resin settles (≈3 min).

steps.title: Wash out unbound bacteria
steps.instruction: Open the column and allow the inoculum to flow out by gravity until dry (≈5 min).

steps.title: Plate flow‑through for enumeration
steps.instruction: Collect the flow‑through, plate on appropriate agar, incubate overnight, and count colonies to determine cells not retained.

steps.title: Plate input inoculum for enumeration
steps.instruction: Plate the original inoculum (parallel) on appropriate agar and incubate overnight for CFU count.

steps.title: Calculate bacterial retention
steps.instruction: Compute bacterial retention as the fraction of cells from the inoculum not recovered in the flow‑through.

steps.title: Grow K12 overnight on agar
steps.instruction: Grow E. coli K12 aerobically overnight on BHI agar at 37 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend colonies to OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.3
steps.instruction: Resuspend colonies of fimbriated and non‑fimbriated K12 in BHI broth to an OD₆₀₀ of approximately 0.3.

steps.title: Grow to OD₆₀₀ > 0.5 and wash
steps.instruction: Incubate until OD₆₀₀ > 0.5, then wash cells in PBS and standardize as described above.

steps.title: Perform affinity assay without competitors
steps.instruction: Prepare columns and bacterial dilutions as previously, then run the affinity assay as before but omit addition of competing sugars.

steps.title: Enumerate colony phenotypes
steps.instruction: Count colonies of fimbriated and non‑fimbriated cells separately from both inocula and assay samples to assess their proportions.
